note: Shared vectors for turning a rate into a whole percentage. Read by tests/test_cli.py and ui/src/viz.test.ts. The rule is HALF-UP: floor(x * 100 + 0.5), which is what JavaScript's Math.round already does and what Python's round() does NOT - round() is banker's rounding, so round(12.5) is 12. Both languages compute this on IEEE doubles, so even the cases where a float is not exactly the half it looks like must come out the same. One file rather than two sets of expectations: a test comparing against a hardcoded string cannot catch a divergence between them.

vectors.why: 12.5% - THE case: Python's round() gives 12, JS Math.round gives 13
0.5% - a half at the bottom of the range; round() would give 0
99.5% - a half at the top, which half-up carries to 100
22.5% - round() gives 22 (2 is even), half-up gives 23
37.5% - round() gives 38 here, so the two rules AGREE; a control
87.5% - round() gives 88, so the two agree again; the second control
a third - no half anywhere near it
two thirds - rounds up on both rules
just under the .5 boundary at 14.49% - down on both
just over it at 14.51% - up on both
11.5% as a float is 11.500000000000002, not 11.5 - the languages must still agree
